sigma.name: SIGMA
sigma.geometry: 128 Flex-DPEs x 128 BF16 multipliers; FP32 accumulation
sigma.onchip_bandwidth_note: Fig.8 labels 960 GB/s data and 120 GB/s bitmap feeds; these are not external bandwidths.
notes: FP8 and INT4 can be widened numerically to BF16; conversion and unpacking time is not supplied.

bitwave.name: BitWave
bitwave.geometry: 512 BCEs x 8 SMMs (1b x 8b); equivalent to 512 dense 8b x 8b MACs/cycle
bitwave.onchip_bandwidth_note: Table I SU1-SU6: W 256-1024 bit/cycle, A 64-1024 bit/cycle. No explicit DRAM data rate was found; SRAM feed must not replace it.
bitwave.reference_precision: INT8 x INT8 capacity proxy; no extra W4 compute packing benefit
bitwave.source_location: BitWave HPCA2024, Sec.IV-C, Table I, Sec.V-A
notes: Native hardware is integer, not FP8. The dense capacity is a proxy, not a lossless FP8 timing model.
Decode utilization=1 is optimistic; the native SU4-SU6 expose only one token and less parallel work than prefill.

ebb_cim.name: EBB-CIM / MulTCIM
ebb_cim.geometry: 16 cores x 8 macros x 32 arrays; each array computes 8 input-bit x INT8-weight products/cycle
ebb_cim.onchip_bandwidth_note: The FPGA DDR3/FMC test platform is described, but an effective chip external bandwidth is not specified in the inspected paper.
ebb_cim.reference_precision: INT8 x INT8 capacity proxy; W4 occupies native 8b weight words
ebb_cim.source_location: MulTCIM JSSC2024, Fig.4, Fig.14, Fig.16, Sec.VII
notes: The reported 3.55 TOPS already includes sparse benefit; dense throughput from the array is 2.2528 TOPS at 275 MHz.
Native INT16 dense throughput is 0.5632 TOPS, a different precision reference. Exact FP8 alignment width/pass costs are not specified here.

bitpragmatic.name: Bit-Pragmatic
bitpragmatic.geometry: 16 tiles x 256 PIPs; each PIP processes 16 oneffset x weight terms/cycle
bitpragmatic.onchip_bandwidth_note: Each tile supplies 256 weight lanes; dispatcher broadcasts activation oneffsets. These widths do not specify external DRAM bandwidth.
bitpragmatic.reference_precision: Original 16b fixed-point dense reference; not the separate 8b reduced-column variant
notes: No explicit absolute clock/data rate was located in the inspected paper; supply the chosen operating point instead of borrowing Bitlet's 1 GHz.
Original PIP columns exploit 16 windows/tokens; using all of them for batch-one decode is an optimistic capacity assumption.
This is not Bitlet. FP8 exponent alignment and control time are not modeled.

asyn_cim.name: Asyn-CIM
asyn_cim.geometry: 16 macros x 16 banks; 384 bit columns/bank = 48 INT8 weight words; paper FP8 mantissa BI=3
asyn_cim.onchip_bandwidth_note: External HBM 1 TB/s; internal refill/replication traffic and weight-update stalls require a separate model.
asyn_cim.reference_precision: Paper FP8 x INT8 dense reference, 8.192 TOPS; W4 external packing does not double compute
asyn_cim.source_location: User-supplied Asyn_CIM_HPCA2027.pdf, Eq.(5), Sec.IV-C, Fig.10, Fig.14, Fig.16
notes: Fig.16 speedup is a sparsity-handling ratio, not E2E speedup; its application to 2048 prefill and decode is an extrapolation.
The 16.90 ms TPOT in Fig.14 is a different traffic/context measurement; it is not imported into this packed-W4 estimate.
